'''''Mackaya bella''''', called the '''forest bell bush''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the acanthus family [[Acanthaceae]], [[native species|native]] to [[South Africa]] ([[Cape Provinces]], [[KwaZulu-Natal]], and [[Northern Provinces]]) and [[Eswatini]].<ref name="52245-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:52245-1 |title=''Mackaya bella'' Harv. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=27 September 2023}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Mackaya bella, blom, Manie van der Schijff BT, b.jpg|thumb|left|Flower]]
Growing to {{convert|1.5|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall and broad, it is an erect, [[evergreen]] shrub with opposite arranged {{Convert|4 to 5|in|cm|adj=on}} long glossy, slim, elliptically-shaped dark green leaves that feature wavy margins and salient midrib and veins on the lower surface.<ref name=sm>[https://www.smgrowers.com/products/plants/plantdisplay.asp?plant_id=1026 Mackaya bella - Forest Bell Bush] San Marcos Growers. Retrieved 19 January 2025.</ref> 

2 inch long, trumpet-shaped, pale lilac to lavender flowers veined in purple appear profusely in spring and early summer. The throats have noticeable deep purple veins.<ref name=sm/> 

==Cultivation==
The plant is not hardy below {{convert|-6|C|F|abbr=on}}, therefore in colder [[temperate climate|temperate]] zones requires protection during the winter months.<ref name=sm/> However, it may be placed outside in a sheltered spot in summer. It requires an [[alkaline soil|alkaline]] or neutral soil.<ref name = RHSPF/> 

It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web|title=''Mackaya bella'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/10659/Mackaya-bella/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=10 November 2020}}</ref>
